cases.name: a listener on a plain target hears a dispatched event
cases.js: var t = new EventTarget(), log = []; t.addEventListener('ping', function (e) { log.push([this === t, e.target === t, e.currentTarget === t, e.eventPhase, e.type].join('/')); }); var e = new Event('ping'); var ret = t.dispatchEvent(e); log.push([ret, e.target === t, e.currentTarget, e.eventPhase].join('/')); log.join()

cases.name: a bubbling event on a plain target does not reach window or document
cases.js: var t = new EventTarget(), log = []; function w() { log.push('window'); } function d() { log.push('document'); } window.addEventListener('zz', w, true); window.addEventListener('zz', w); document.addEventListener('zz', d); t.addEventListener('zz', function (e) { log.push('target:' + e.composedPath().length); }); t.dispatchEvent(new Event('zz', { bubbles: true })); window.removeEventListener('zz', w, true); window.removeEventListener('zz', w); document.removeEventListener('zz', d); log.join()

cases.name: capture and bubble listeners both run at the target, in order added
cases.js: var t = new EventTarget(), log = []; t.addEventListener('x', function () { log.push('bubble'); }); t.addEventListener('x', function () { log.push('capture'); }, true); t.dispatchEvent(new Event('x')); log.join()
cases.gap: the engine runs capture listeners first at the target, as DOM 2.9 has it and as Chrome does for a node; Chrome runs a non-node target's listeners in the order added

cases.name: once, removeEventListener and the same listener twice
cases.js: var t = new EventTarget(), n = 0, m = 0, k = 0; function a() { n++; } function b() { m++; } function c() { k++; } t.addEventListener('x', a, { once: true }); t.addEventListener('x', b); t.addEventListener('x', b); t.addEventListener('x', c); t.removeEventListener('x', c); t.dispatchEvent(new Event('x')); t.dispatchEvent(new Event('x')); [n, m, k].join()

cases.js: var t = new EventTarget(); t.addEventListener('x', function (e) { e.preventDefault(); }); [t.dispatchEvent(new Event('x', { cancelable: true })), t.dispatchEvent(new Event('x'))].join()

cases.name: a subclass with private fields, a static instance and an Event subclass (github react-core router state)
cases.js: var NAME = 'router:state-update'; class Update extends Event { constructor() { super(NAME); } } class Store extends EventTarget { static #one; #state = null; constructor() { super(); } static getInstance() { return Store.#one || (Store.#one = new Store()), Store.#one; } getState() { return this.#state; } setState(s) { this.#state = s; this.dispatchEvent(new Update()); } subscribe(f) { var c = new AbortController(); this.addEventListener(NAME, () => { f(this.#state); }, { signal: c.signal }); f(this.#state); return () => { c.abort(); }; } } var s = Store.getInstance(), log = []; var stop = s.subscribe(function (v) { log.push(String(v)); }); s.setState('a'); s.setState('b'); stop(); s.setState('c'); [log.join('|'), s === Store.getInstance(), s.getState()].join()
